planner_json.title: Qualify the claude-code 2.1.291 table on hosted captures
provides: the qualified table claude-code@2.1.291 with its archived captures
consumes: E1 rule vocabulary and capture-set qualification
boundary_contracts: captured bytes to table state: claude-code@2.1.291 qualifies only on real bytes at exactly that version, and any change to those bytes or rules stops it qualifying
depends_on: E1 (the capture-set qualification and the table schema this table must satisfy)
GAW-9 (AC-1 needs its exported captures at 2.1.291; no locked flow replays it)

write_prohibited: test/harness/stream/*.mjs - E1 owns the normaliser and qualification; a table is data
test/harness/graders/** - E1 and E2 own grading
test/harness/adapters/** - GAW-1 owns the adapter contract

archived_captures.description: Real stdout bytes from a hosted run at the exact pinned CLI version, committed with hashes and source run id
records: its capture record, whose stdout sha256 equals those bytes

specification.objective: The claude-code 2.1.291 table qualifies on real hosted captures at exactly that version, with the question fact read as agent text when no question tool is offered.
specification.success_state: Table claude-code@2.1.291 computes to state qualified from real captures at exactly that version, with all 6 required facts citing an offset and a sha256.

requirements.title: The claude-code 2.1.291 table qualifies on real captures, and stops when its bytes or rules change
requirements.description: GIVEN `archived_captures`, real claude-code stdout at exactly 2.1.291 from a hosted run, with hashes and the source run id WHEN qualification is computed from them, then on temp copies with one changed byte, one removed rule and another declared version THEN state reads qualified with all 6 required facts citing offsets, a changed byte reads capture-citation-mismatch, a removed rule reads required-fact-unmapped, and another version reads stream-mapping-absent
requirements.positive_example: Real captures of status, verify, init and the denied-write probe at 2.1.291: table state qualified, with each of the 6 required facts citing an offset and a sha256.
requirements.red: On base the table reads qualified false and cites only a keyless 2.1.312 capture, so its state reads unqualified and this test fails.
requirements.verification_service: real claude-code 2.1.291 stdout bytes captured on a hosted run, through the real normaliser and validator

scenario.verification_service: real claude-code 2.1.291 stdout bytes captured on a hosted run, through the real normaliser and validator

would_fail_if: the table is empty or holds a catch-all rule
the capture is hand-written instead of captured from the real CLI
qualified is a stored boolean with no capture behind it

build_proof.range: anything that proves the claude-code table at exactly 2.1.291 maps every required fact to spans of real captured bytes, and that it stops qualifying when those bytes or rules change

steps: load claude-code@2.1.291 and compute its qualification from its archived captures
change one byte of one archived capture in a temp copy and recompute
remove the rule for one required fact in a temp copy and recompute
normalise the archived capture against a temp table declaring another version

must_observe: table state `qualified` with all `6` required facts, each citing an offset and a sha256
rule removed: reason `required-fact-unmapped` naming that fact
must_not_observe: an empty offsets list on a fact the table declares observed
